author: TeIq
content:
## Source
.design/m5/49-hardware-token-signing.md — full design.

## What this epic delivers
Sixth `SigningKey` impl using hardware tokens (PKCS#11 + FIDO2 PRF). Two operational modes: **attended-batch** (operator periodically signs queued labels via CLI) and **attended-realtime** (separate `polaris-signer` daemon holds the token + accepts signing RPCs). Key generated inside the token; signing requires physical presence (touch). Strongest at-rest custody mode in the matrix.

## Hard constraints
- **`SigningError::WouldBlock` is the abstraction** — the trait extension that lets the impl say "no signer reachable right now." Pending labels enter `signature_status = 'PendingSignature'` and emit after async sign.
- **`secrecy::SecretString` for PINs** — never on disk, never in logs, zeroed on Drop. Per rust-quality §6.
- **No software key material exists** — generation happens INSIDE the token; `C_Sign` returns only the signature. Audit via strace/equivalent confirms no read of key bytes from token memory.

## Sub-issues (10 PRs + 1 Q-resolution)
- Q-resolution: batch vs realtime priority (Q1), FIDO2 vs PKCS#11 default (Q2), PIN UX (Q3), batch touch policy (Q4), N-of-M quorum (Q5), daemon transport (Q6)
- PR 1: `SigningError::WouldBlock` + `PhysicalPresenceTimeout` + `TokenDisconnected` variants (additive; foundation)
- PR 2: `HwTokenSigningKey` impl, batch mode, PKCS#11 backend via `cryptoki` + softhsm2 fixture; AC-1
- PR 3: `labels.signature_status` schema + `signed_at` + `pending_label_queue` view; AC-2 enabling
- PR 4: `polaris labeler-sign-pending` CLI binding (end-to-end batch flow); AC-2 end-to-end
- PR 5: `polaris-signer` daemon (new workspace binary) with gRPC over TLS-mutual-auth (Q6-A)
- PR 6: backend realtime client connecting to the daemon + disconnect/reconnect handling; AC-3
- PR 7: FIDO2 PRF backend via `ctap-hid-fido2` (touch-per-sign); AC-6
- PR 8: `polaris labeler-key rotate` hardware-token-mode extension; AC-8
- PR 9: `docs/operations/hardware-token-signing.md` operator runbook (token init, PIN management, token-loss recovery)
- PR 10: AC-5 + AC-7 audit closure (strace verification + miri)

## Provisional answers
- Q1: A (ship batch first; realtime in follow-up PRs 5-6) — batch is shippable sooner; realtime needs more infra
- Q2: C (both, config-selectable; PKCS#11 default — hits more existing operator hardware)
- Q3: A for PKCS#11 (PIN at daemon start; `secrecy` crate); D for FIDO2 (touch instead of PIN)
- Q4: A (touch-per-sign required in batch mode; weakening defeats the point); revisit if operators say 100-touches-per-batch is unworkable
- Q5: A (single-token v2; quorum is its own follow-up issue with key ceremony design)
- Q6: A (gRPC over TLS-mutual-auth — `tonic` lands anyway via ML epic; reuse)

## Rust-quality notes for downstream
- **`SigningError` extension is additive** — the variant is new; existing v1 impls never return it; existing call sites are unaffected. Per rust-quality §1: this is the right way to extend an enum.
- **PIN secrets via `secrecy::SecretString`** — wraps `String` so Debug never prints the value; provides explicit `.expose_secret()` for the one PKCS#11 `C_Login` call site. Per rust-quality §6.
- **`cryptoki` session lifetime**: hold one session per token, scoped by `Drop` to close cleanly. Per rust-quality §10: never hold a session handle across `.await` — PKCS#11 calls are synchronous; wrap in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
- **`polaris-signer` daemon TLS-mutual-auth**: client cert pinned in the daemon's config; daemon cert pinned in the backend's config. Cert rotation is operator-driven. Per rust-quality §9: the daemon and the backend share a tonic-generated proto crate for the wire schema.
- **`pending_label_signer` background worker**: per-classifier pattern from ML epic (#127) applies here too. `JoinSet`, cancel-safe `select!`, idempotent retries on `WouldBlock`.
- **Audit-friendliness**: every sign call emits `tracing::info_span!("sign", action_id = %action.id, mode = "hwtoken", touch_required = %config.touch_required)`. Operators can grep for touch failures.

## External references
- `cryptoki` (PKCS#11): https://docs.rs/cryptoki/latest/cryptoki/
- `ctap-hid-fido2`: https://docs.rs/ctap-hid-fido2/latest/ctap_hid_fido2/
- `secrecy` crate: https://docs.rs/secrecy/latest/secrecy/
- `softhsm2` fixture: https://github.com/opendnssec/SoftHSMv2
- TLS mutual auth with `rustls`: https://docs.rs/rustls/latest/rustls/

## Blocks / blocked-by
- Independent of all other M5 epics. Complementary to #152 TPM signing (TPM = unattended local; hwtoken = attended portable; two different operator postures).
